title: Console: add Cost Model API client + request caching (feature-flagged) and metrics
author: Chloe Martin
description:
Summary: This PR wires the Console backend to the new Cost Model API (SCM) via a typed client, adds a small request-level caching layer to keep p95 down on hot pages, and introduces feature-flagged rollout + metrics so we can canary per-tenant without regressing the cost breakdown page.

Background / why: Console cost breakdown needs deterministic, explainable cost attribution across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. The Cost Model service provides this, but Console needs: (1) strict validation + version negotiation, (2) conservative timeouts with graceful fallback, (3) caching to avoid repeated explain calls for the same (tenant, route, window) when users refresh or paginate, and (4) observability to detect slowdowns/timeouts before impacting the UI.

What changed: Added a new CostModelClient with version negotiation headers (X-Redwood-CostModel-Version-Requested, X-Redwood-CostModel-Version-Accept) and consistent error mapping; implemented a per-process LRU+TTL cache keyed by (tenant_id, scm_version, request_hash) with safe scoping to prevent cross-tenant leakage; added a circuit-breaker style fast-fail when the downstream is timing out (opens after N failures in rolling window, cool-down before half-open); updated Console cost breakdown handler to call /v1/cost-model/estimate for summary cards and /v1/cost-model/explain for tooltips/drilldown payload (still behind flag); added metrics: latency histogram by endpoint, error counts by normalized error_code, cache hit ratio, circuit breaker state transitions, and fallback usage rate.

Flags / rollout: console_cost_breakdown_use_scm (default off) gates calling SCM at all; console_cost_breakdown_scm_cache_enabled (default on when SCM is on) gates request cache; console_cost_breakdown_scm_explain_enabled (default off) gates explain endpoint usage (estimate-only mode remains available). Flags are evaluated per-tenant with allowlist support.

Timeouts / retries: client timeout 250ms (configurable), 1 retry on transport-level errors only (no retries on validation/unsupported_version), and request hedging is explicitly NOT enabled for now (avoid double-spend load on SCM). Fallback behavior: if SCM is unavailable/slow, Console returns legacy computed totals where available and marks breakdown sections as "Estimated (limited)" with an internal reason code for support/debugging.

Security / logging: Do not log request payloads (they include tenant-level dimensions and route identifiers). We log only: tenant_id, request_id, scm_version, endpoint, and normalized error_code. Actor metadata (user_id/service) is passed through via headers for audit correlation (X-Redwood-Actor-Id, X-Redwood-Actor-Type) but never stored in cache keys.

Tests: Added unit tests for cache key scoping + TTL expiry, client error mapping, and circuit breaker state transitions. Added integration test stub behind feature flag for staging (skipped in local runs unless SCM_STAGING_URL is set).

Follow-ups: (1) switch cache backend to shared (redis) if we see too much variance across pods; (2) flip explain flag once payload size constraints are finalized; (3) add dashboard panels in Console service Grafana for fallback rate + SCM p95 (tracked in ENG-23217).

Release notes: Internal-only. No customer billing changes; this only affects Console cost breakdown display, gated by feature flags and allowlist.
commits: console: introduce cost-model client interface + HTTP implementation
console: add scoped LRU TTL cache for SCM requests
console: wire cost breakdown handler to SCM estimate/explain (feature-flagged)
console: metrics + structured logs for SCM dependency
console: circuit breaker + conservative retry policy
tests: cache scoping, version negotiation, error mapping
docs: internal notes on flags, timeouts, and fallback behavior
conversation: Priya Natarajan: Please confirm we’re using the same version negotiation scheme as ADR-0147 (requested vs accept headers). Also make sure unsupported version is distinguishable from invalid inputs so Console can avoid retry storms.

Chloe Martin (author): Yep. Client sets X-Redwood-CostModel-Version-Requested and X-Redwood-CostModel-Version-Accept (comma-separated). Unsupported version maps to SCM_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION and we do not retry. Validation maps to SCM_INVALID_ARGUMENT and we surface a safe fallback.
Jordan Lee: Cache key should include resolved scm_version (post-negotiation) not just requested. Otherwise clients requesting v2 but falling back to v1 could contaminate cache entries.

Chloe Martin (author): Good catch. Updated cache key to include response header X-Redwood-CostModel-Version-Used. Added unit test: requested=v2, used=v1 yields distinct key from requested=v1, used=v1.

Sean Gallagher: Timeout 250ms feels tight but OK for a dependent call. Please add metric for fallback rate and a counter for circuit breaker open -> this will help oncall. Also ensure we have a hard cap on cache size to avoid memory surprises.

Chloe Martin (author): Added fallback_rate metric and breaker_state_transition counter. Cache is capped at 5k entries per pod with per-entry size guard (reject caching responses >256KB). TTL default 30s.
Jada Williams: Any risk of cross-tenant leakage with caching? I want explicit code-level scoping and a test.
Chloe Martin (author): Cache key includes tenant_id and environment (region) and we never cache if tenant_id is missing. Added test to assert different tenants do not share entries.
Felix Schneider: Please ensure logs do not include route names/prompt identifiers. Support will need correlation though—do we have request_id + tenant_id + scm_version in every log line?

Chloe Martin (author): Logs are structured with request_id, tenant_id, endpoint, scm_version_used, and normalized error_code only. Route IDs are not logged. Correlation is via request_id propagated from gateway.
Dylan Brooks: Looks good. One request: keep explain endpoint behind a separate flag so we can launch estimate-only first (payload sizes still in flux).
Chloe Martin (author): Done: console_cost_breakdown_scm_explain_enabled added and defaults to off. Handler uses estimate-only path unless enabled.
Priya Natarajan: Approved after the cache-key fix + explicit no-retry on unsupported_version/invalid_argument.
Sean Gallagher: Approved. Please link a follow-up for dashboards in ENG-23217 (not blocking).
Dylan Brooks: Approved, ship behind allowlist only.
release_notes: Console backend can optionally fetch cost breakdown estimates from SCM (Cost Model API) behind tenant-scoped feature flags.
Adds request caching + circuit breaker and emits dependency metrics (latency/errors/cache hit/fallback rate).
No billing changes; UI behavior remains unchanged for tenants without the flag.
